newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-LE SAUX'S RECOVERY HAND IN HAND WITH BLACKBURN'S.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-LE SAUX'S RECOVERY HAND IN HAND WITH BLACKBURN'S.

text.p: Kevin Gallacher scored a hat-trick on Saturday to steer Blackburn to a 3-1 win over Wimbledon and the heady heights of 12th place in the English premier league.

It may not seem too impressive at first glance but when it is considered that the Lancashire side, champions in 1995 and seventh last season, were anchored in the relegation zone until January, it represents an impressive recovery.
Now seven points clear of the 18th place that spells division one football next season, Blackburn can begin to relax after a tumultuous season.
Manager Ray Harford resigned in October with the club firmly rooted at the foot of the table, without a league win to their name and dumped out of the League Cup by second division Stockport.
Tony Parkes took over as caretaker manager and the club signed up Swede Sven-Goran Eriksson, currently in charge of Italy's Sampdoria, to take over at the end of the season.
But after weeks of unsettling speculation, Eriksson decided to stay in Italy and instead Blackburn announced that Internazionale boss Roy Hodgson would be the new manager.
Meanwhile, as all the discussions were going on behind the scenes, Parkes and his players were gradually hauling themselves out of trouble.
It all began with a 3-0 victory over Liverpool in November, followed by a run of 10 games with only one defeat.
The recovery coincided exactly with the return of England full back Graeme Le Saux who had been out of action for 14 months after sustaining an awful injury.
Le Saux broke his fibula, dislocated his ankle and ruptured tendons in a freak accident in a league match when his studs caught in the turf.
He fought his way back to fitness and his performances not only helped stabilise Blackburn but earned him a recall to the England side for February's match against Italy.
And after Saturday's win, the Channel Islander was in buoyant mood.
"Today was a really good performance," he said. "We've done well since Tony took over and now we've got something to build on.
"We've had six wins and five draws in the last 12 and a couple more victories will secure us a mid-table position."
It must have been difficult for 28-year-old Le Saux to have to watch from the sidelines as his team mates struggled so badly early in the season, but he says the dark period should not be forgotten.
"After the success we had previously it's important to learn from this season - it's not been good," he said.
Barring a major collapse, Blackburn should stay safely in the top flight and start afresh next season.
Le Saux, who joined Blackburn from Chelsea when Kenny Dalglish was in charge, is looking forward to it and has high hopes for Hodgson.

"I don't know him but he's obviously got great quality," he said of the Englishman who has guided Inter to the top three in serie A. "The clubs he's been with, and especially what he did with Switzerland, speaks for itself and it'll be very exciting.
But whether Le Saux will be around to see the excitement at close hand looks increasingly unlikely.
He reportedly had talks with Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger this week with a view to returning south.
He dismissed the story as "paper talk" on Saturday but it looks ever more likely that the next season at Ewood Park will be played without the man who has done so much to save this one.
